demonstrates: The explicit re-collection request shape (ADR 0007). Ordinary incremental sync moves forward from a cursor and never revisits settled objects, so raising the media-type include set or the size threshold cannot pick up a previously skipped attachment as a side effect of a normal sync. 'recollect_targets' names the one known source object from transcript 15 whose video attachment was declined, with no cursor and no window: the Field re-evaluates that object's attachments against the now-widened policy and re-emits it with the video staged. Core installs the update in place under the object's existing Note ID, per A1 section 7's ordinary current-state update rule -- no new identity behavior is needed.
notes: This transcript specifies the protocol shape only. The re-collection operation itself -- finding Notes that carry skipped_attachments and issuing this request for them -- is 0.1.1 sync-command scope and is not built by A2.

note: No cursor and no window: recollection is scoped exactly to recollect_targets, not to a cursor-bounded incremental range. video/mp4 now appears in artifact_media_types, which is why the Field can stage it this time.

body.text:
# Team standup recording

Hi Sam,

Sharing this week's standup notes and the recording.

Alice

Attachments:
- notes.txt, 40 bytes, retained locally.
- team-standup-recording.mp4, now retained: the media-type include set widened to admit video/mp4.

detail: Core resolves handles 'a0021' and 'a0023' inside the staging directory and streams both.
video/mp4 now clears the widened media-type policy, so the previously-declined attachment is installed at its content-addressed path alongside the already-retained text attachment.

Core locates the current Note by the recollected object's portable exact-source key and rewrites it in place under the same Note ID: an ordinary A1 section 7 current-state update, not a new identity. skipped_attachments no longer names this attachment, because it is now retained.

note: A recollection run's checkpoint is a durability barrier for this run's own records exactly as an ordinary run's is; whether it also advances the Field's primary incremental cursor is a sync-command policy question outside A2's scope.

detail: The updated Note and its artifacts are all durable, so the checkpoint commits.
